newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX NIKKEI FUTURES PARE LOSSES, STILL BEARISH.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX NIKKEI FUTURES PARE LOSSES, STILL BEARISH.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures erased most of their early losses by Wednesday's close but dealers said the market continued to be afflicted by poor sentiment and worries about Japan's economic recovery.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract ended 75 points easier at 19,045 after hitting a low of 18,810.
A late rally in Japanese construction shares after Mitsui Construction Co announced it had reached agreement on its restructuring plan boosted the 225-share Nikkei average.
SIMEX dealers said the September Nikkei's failure to close above the 19,200 level for three straight days pointed to further declines in the near term.
"As long as it doesn't close above 19,200, we're still on a downtrend," a trader at a Japanese brokerage said.
He said the September Nikkei would be supported initially at 18,780 and more solidly at 18,500, but a breach of that level could expose it to a further 1,000-points decline.
Taiwan stock index futures skidded below the 400 points level to close sharply lower as Taipei shares lost 2.57 percent on late selling triggered by Wall Street's overnight drop.
The August MSCI contract lost 16.5 points to close at 397.3 on volume of 3,076 lots.
